title: Monetizing Platforms: An Empirical Analysis of Supply and Demand Responses to Entry Costs in Two-Sided Markets
eligible_reason: The demand-side analysis (Tables 4-5, Figures 10-11) is a staggered-adoption design: each book enters a Goodreads giveaway in a book-specific month (giveaway_yearmon; 51 distinct months from 2016-01 to 2020-03 among 81,608 books, one giveaway per book in the shipped panel) and post_giveaway = 1 for book-months after that month. Table 4 column (2) for review volume, Table 4 column (1) for average rating and Table 5 column (1) for the share of fit-related negative reviews regress the book-month outcome on post_giveaway alone with book and year-month fixed effects, clustered by book, no covariates, in a window of 12 months before/after the book's own giveaway (lfe::felm). Figure 11 reports Callaway-Sant'Anna att_gt estimates (did package) of the same treatment with Goodreads 'similar books' that never ran a giveaway as the never-treated control group, separately for pre- and post-monetization giveaways. Ineligible parts: the Post Giveaway x Post Monetization interaction columns (subgroup-by-treatment interaction, post_mon is a book-level indicator for giveaways after January 2018); Figure 10 (event-time regressions with relative-month FE only, no unit FE); the supply-side Table 2 (two-period publisher DiD around the single January 2018 monetization date with 2015-2016 as a placebo control period) and the genre Table 3 (single date x genre-group interactions). Caveats for the lead: in the TWFE samples every book is eventually treated (comparison from not-yet-treated books only, event-window sample); the CSA control group is a pre-selected set of 'similar' non-giveaway books (one per focal book), which is a chosen comparison group rather than statistical matching.
design_notes: Package MS_replication_package (valid _archive zip, 982 MB; pipeline extracted it to package_dir at 14:44). Demand code code/demand/02_demand_results.R: review_vol_yearmon.Rds (12.6M book-months, 81,608 books, yearmon 2008-02 to 2020-12) -> u_sub = diff_month in [-12, 12]; felm(N ~ post_giveaway | book_id + yearmon | 0 | book_id). Ratings panel ratings_cleaned.Rds (review-level; avg_r_yearmon by book-month) is referenced but NOT in the zip; the review-level file latest_fulldata_Category_Prediction.csv (885 MB) carries book_id, time, star_rating, yearmon, post_giveaway, giveaway_yearmon, diff_month and the BERT fit category, so the rating and fit panels can be rebuilt from it. CSA (code-raw-data/demand_data_cleaning_code.R lines 301-376): att_gt(yname N or avg_r_yearmon, tname ym_num, idname focal_book_id, gname giveaways_ym_num (0 for similar control books), control_group 'nevertreated', allow_unbalanced_panel, clustervar focal_book_id, anticipation = 1 for volume), run on post_mon == 0 and post_mon == 1 samples; aggte simple and dynamic. The fitted MP objects are shipped (vol_premon_attgt_similarcontrol.gz 287 MB, vol_postmon_attgt_similarcontrol.gz 121 MB, postmon_attgt_simcontrol.gz 78 MB; premon_attgt_simcontrol missing); did MP objects embed DIDparams$data, so the focal+similar panels may be recoverable from them. Supply Table 2: felm(ncount ~ treated:after + treated:after:big5Publishing | month + cleanPublisherAfter | 0 | cleanPublisher) on publisher-months 2015-2018 (treated = 2017-2018, after = 2016 or 2018). Genre Table 3: felm(proportion ~ post2:above_q75 + post2:below_q25 | genre + month).
n_eligible_specs_note: 3 TWFE columns (Table 4 volume col 2, Table 4 rating col 1, Table 5 col 1) + 4 CSA estimates in Figure 11 (volume and rating x pre- and post-monetization samples).
n_adoption_cohorts_note: Computed from review_vol_yearmon.Rds: 51 distinct giveaway_yearmon values (2016-01 .. 2020-03), largest cohorts about 2,500-3,000 books each; one giveaway month per book. Pre-monetization sample: 24 cohorts (2016-2017); post-monetization: 27 cohorts (2018-2020-03).
never_treated_note: TWFE samples contain only giveaway books (all eventually treated; not-yet-treated comparisons within the +/-12-month windows). CSA samples add never-treated 'similar' books (gname = 0).
modern_estimators_named: callaway_santanna (did::att_gt, control_group nevertreated, aggte simple and dynamic)
